class.name: NetwClockCore
class.brief_description: Tick engine behind [ClockCore]: it turns frame deltas into a fixed-rate tick schedule, keeps that schedule aligned with a server's, and decides which frames the simulated world may advance on.
class.description:
A tick is a fixed amount of simulated time, and everything here follows from that one commitment. The schedule converts frame deltas into whole ticks and banks the remainder, so two half frames are worth exactly one tick and no time is invented or lost. This engine holds no [Object] and sends nothing. The ping and pong messages that carry a latency sample, and the node that authors the configuration, both live in [ClockCore] above it. That is why calibration is fed rather than fetched: [method handle_pong] takes a sample somebody else received, and answers what the peer should now believe. [ClockCore] owns the one instance a session has and is the surface to use. Reach for this class directly only when writing the clock itself. [codeblock] var clock := NetwClockCore.new() clock.tickrate = 30
clock.physics_step(delta) # pumped once per physics frame clock.force_step(1) # or stepped, for a deterministic rig # clock.tick advanced either way, and emitted the same signals [/codeblock] [method physics_step] and [method force_step] emit identically, so a stepped rig and a running session cannot mean different things by a tick. They differ in one respect and it is a law rather than an oversight: a step is not a frame, so [method force_step] brackets no [signal before_tick_loop]. The simulation gate is the part that is easy to mistake for a detail. The physics server runs exactly one step per frame and takes no argument about how long that step is, so the only way a clock can make a tick worth the same amount of time on two peers is to decide which frames the world may step at all. A gated clock pays each tick into a budget of whole steps and spends one per simulated frame, and a frame with nothing to spend holds. [codeblock] arm_gate() a body the physics server integrates tick emitted -> credit += physics_steps_per_tick() frame spends -> credit -= 1, is_simulating() true no credit -> is_simulating() false, the world holds release_gate() the last release restores every frame [/codeblock] A gated clock emits at most one tick per frame, because a second tick would have to share the single step the physics server runs. A peer that cannot sustain that rate therefore cannot catch up by doubling a frame: it falls behind and says so through [method simulation_behind_count], and sustained growth there means the peer is too slow to predict, which no netcode setting repairs. Calibration keeps the schedule aligned with a server's without ever teleporting the playhead. [constant SYNC_SNAP] takes the whole correction at once. [constant SYNC_STRETCH] takes a fraction of it per frame, falling back to a snap once the divergence passes [member panic_snap_threshold], which is a real desync rather than drift. The target is a continuous clock position rather than a whole tick, and that is deliberate. Rounding the tick phase [method handle_pong] takes away would make the target jump by a full tick as a ping's arrival phase slid across a server boundary, and [constant SYNC_STRETCH] would then chase that sawtooth for about a second at a time, dragging the local tick boundary back and forth through the server's. The margin that used to ride on that rounding is [member lead_ticks], which is explicit.

method.name: arm_gate
method.description: Arms one gate, held until [method release_gate]. Gates nest, because two predicted bodies in one session share one clock and either may leave first. The clock decides whether a frame advances simulated time. It never touches a physics space itself, because it has no scene: the caller arms a gate when it registers a body the physics server integrates, reads [method is_simulating] after the tick loop, and holds that body's space.

method.name: clear
method.description: Restarts the session: the tick, the calibration, the sample window, the gates and the step budget all return to what a fresh engine holds.

method.name: consume_ping_due
method.description: Accumulates the ping cadence, returning [code]true[/code] and rearming once [member ping_interval] has elapsed. The engine sends nothing, so the pump above it owns the send and this only says when one is due.

method.name: display_tick
method.description: The tick a visual should render, [member tick] less [member display_offset], never below zero.

method.name: force_step
method.description: Synchronously emits [param count] whole ticks without consulting real time, so a deterministic rig owns the schedule instead of the frame pump. It emits exactly what [method physics_step] emits per tick, so a stepped run and a pumped one agree. A step is not a frame, so no tick-loop bracket fires. Call it with zero to spend a frame that ran no tick, which is what a gated stepper owes the gate.

method.name: handle_pong
method.description: Ingests one round-trip [param sample] and the server clock position it was measured against, recalibrates, and answers the metrics the surface above publishes. [param server_tick_phase] is the server's position within [param server_tick_at_pong], at or above zero and below one, so the target is a continuous clock position rather than a whole tick. [param apply_lead] is [code]false[/code] for a server echoing its own probe: it has no flight time to its own authority and so never leads itself. Every other peer adds half its averaged round trip plus [member lead_ticks]. [codeblock] { ┠╴rtt_raw (float) the sample just ingested ┠╴rtt_avg (float) averaged over the window ┠╴rtt_jitter (float) mean absolute deviation ┠╴diff (int) ticks the target was off by ┠╴tick (int) where the clock now sits ┠╴display_offset (int) what is configured ┠╴recommended_display_offset (int) what conditions suggest ┠╴is_stable (bool) jitter under the threshold ┖╴is_synchronized (bool) a calibration has landed } [/codeblock]

method.name: is_gated
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while any gate armed by [method arm_gate] is still held.

method.name: is_simulating
method.description: Whether this frame's simulated world may advance. Stays [code]true[/code] for a whole session unless a gate is armed, so a game that predicts nothing never sees a held frame.

method.name: is_stable
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while [method rtt_jitter] is below [member jitter_stability_threshold].

method.name: one_way_latency
method.description: Half the averaged round trip, in seconds: the estimate a display offset is sized against.

method.name: physics_factor
method.description: The engine's physics rate over [member tickrate]. Scales velocities authored per tick into the per-step units the physics server integrates.

method.name: physics_step
method.description: Advances the schedule by one frame worth [param delta] seconds, emitting whole ticks and banking the remainder. A [param delta] above [member stall_threshold] is a hitch rather than simulated time, so whatever was banked before it is discarded instead of being paid out as a burst. At most [member max_ticks_per_frame] ticks are emitted, or exactly one while a gate is armed.

method.name: physics_steps_per_tick
method.description: [method physics_factor] as a whole number, never below one. The physics server runs exactly one step per frame, so a tick can be worth one step or two but never one and a fifth. A fractional factor is a declaration the engine cannot honour, and the step budget rounds it here rather than pretending otherwise.

method.name: recommended_display_offset
method.description: The [member display_offset] current conditions call for: one-way latency plus jitter scaled by [member jitter_multiplier], in ticks. Answers [member display_offset] unchanged until a calibration has landed, since there is nothing yet to base a recommendation on.

method.name: release_gate
method.description: Releases one gate armed by [method arm_gate]. The last release restores an ungated clock, which simulates every frame, rather than leaving the world held on whatever the final decision happened to be. Releasing past zero is not a negative gate.

method.name: rtt
method.description: The latest round-trip sample in seconds, unaveraged.

method.name: rtt_avg
method.description: The round trip averaged over the last [member jitter_window] samples, in seconds.

method.name: rtt_jitter
method.description: Mean absolute deviation of the sample window, in seconds. This is what decides [method is_stable] and what widens [method recommended_display_offset].

method.name: simulation_behind_count
method.description: How many frames wanted a tick the gate's ceiling refused. A gated clock emits one tick per frame at most, so a peer whose physics cannot sustain [member tickrate] times [method physics_steps_per_tick] steps per wall second cannot catch up. Sustained growth here means this peer is too slow to predict.

method.name: tick_accumulator
method.description: The unspent remainder in seconds, unclamped. A visual playhead reads this rather than [method tick_phase]. If a render frame lands just after a physics frame the remainder can exceed one whole tick, and clamping it there stalls the playhead for the rest of that frame, which shows up as a jitter the clamp itself caused.

method.name: tick_phase
method.description: Where the clock sits inside its current tick, clamped to the range zero through one. This is the phase a server echoes with its tick so a client can calibrate against a continuous position. Clamped because it rides the wire as a fraction of one tick, unlike [method tick_accumulator].

method.name: ticktime
method.description: The duration of a single tick in seconds, the reciprocal of [member tickrate].

members.member: How many ticks the visual display lags behind the simulation. Compare against [method recommended_display_offset].
The jitter below which the connection reads as stable.
How many recent round-trip samples are averaged. The window is what lets an outlier age back out.

Ticks a client's clock deliberately leads its half-round-trip estimate by, the margin that gets an input authored for server tick [code]T[/code] to the server before it consumes [code]T[/code]. Too small and the server's consume cursor runs dry; too large and every input waits that much longer to be simulated. Ignored when [method handle_pong] is called with [code]apply_lead[/code] false.
The most ticks one [method physics_step] may emit. A gate overrides it down to one.
The divergence in ticks past which [constant SYNC_STRETCH] stops crawling and snaps. A gap this size is a real desync rather than drift.
Seconds between latency probes, measured by [method consume_ping_due].
The frame delta above which [method physics_step] discards what was banked, treating the frame as a hitch rather than as simulated time.
The fraction of the remaining divergence [constant SYNC_STRETCH] closes each frame.
How the local clock aligns with the server, one of [enum SyncMode].
Whether a calibration has landed. The first [method handle_pong] sets it and hard-aligns, so [constant SYNC_STRETCH] begins already converged.
The current server-calibrated simulation tick. Settable because a peer that has not calibrated yet is placed rather than advanced.
How many simulation ticks run per second. Every derived duration comes from this.

signal.name: after_tick
signal.description: Emitted at the end of each tick, after game logic.

signal.name: after_tick_loop
signal.description: Emitted once after [method physics_step]'s tick loop finishes, whether or not it emitted a tick. Not emitted by [method force_step], which is a step rather than a frame.

signal.name: before_tick
signal.description: Emitted at the start of each tick, before game logic.

signal.name: before_tick_loop
signal.description: Emitted once before [method physics_step]'s tick loop runs, whether or not it will emit a tick. Not emitted by [method force_step], which is a step rather than a frame.

signal.name: clock_synchronized
signal.description: Emitted once, when the first calibration lands. A later [method handle_pong] recalibrates without re-announcing.

signal.name: display_offset_insufficient
signal.description: Emitted when [method recommended_display_offset] rises above [member display_offset]. Latched, so worsening conditions do not repeat it, and it can fire again once conditions recover and degrade a second time.

signal.name: on_tick
signal.description: Emitted during each tick. Primary simulation logic connects here.

signal.name: stability_changed
signal.description: Emitted when [method is_stable] flips, so a listener sees the transition rather than having to poll for it.

constants.constant: Hard-jump the local tick to the calibrated target on every sample.
Nudge the accumulator toward the target a fraction at a time, so the playhead never teleports, falling back to a snap once the divergence exceeds [member panic_snap_threshold].
